text:
Ada: Heads-up — after last week's burst we saw a cascade of cross-AZ scale-downs that tripped network egress and caused long pod startup (T > 2m). Thinking we should experiment with 'AZ fencing' in the autoscaler to avoid scaling down below X nodes per-AZ. Anyone else seen this?

Sam: Saw it too. Pods stayed Pending while new node spun up in different AZ. Can you paste the numbers?

Ada: Sure — during the event: 14 scale-down actions in 8m, ~65% of them caused pod groups to move across AZs. Median pod startup + kube-proxy init ~82s, CNI attach ~40s. Cross-AZ egress jumped ~30%.

Mikel: Sounds like ENI / subnet IP exhaustion + conntrack/kube-proxy warm-up. Also our node pools have different maxPods settings — fragmentation makes autoscaler pick suboptimal pools. We should avoid draining the AZ that still has spare IPs.

Rachel: Proposed flags we can try (canary in eu-west1):

```
--expander=least-waste \\n--scale-down-enabled=true \\n--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m \\n--scale-down-unready-time=20m \\n--max-empty-bulk-delete=1 \\n--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false \\n--balance-similar-node-groups=true \\n--az-availability-fence=1  # custom patch in our fork
```

Ada: FYI our fork exposes `--az-availability-fence` which enforces a minimum node count per AZ during scale-down. Branch: autoscaler/az-fence.

Jess: Also recommend adjusting `--ok-total-unready-count` and adding a node annotation to prevent eviction for model-serving pods for a short window (5m) during scale events.

Mikel: We should consider an expander tweak: prefer filling existing nodes in the same AZ ("prefer-complete-node") to reduce pod spreading. For preemptible mixes, use price-awareness so bursts prefer non-preemptible pools.

Sam: Can we define a clear canary? My proposal: eu-west1 canary, nodepool sizes 6/6/6 (az-balanced), set `az-availability-fence=2`, `scale-down-unneeded-time=15m`, collect metrics: time-to-ready, egress bytes, pod-moves. Run 24h and compare to baseline.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: `autoscaler-config/autoscaler-eu-canary` applied by Jess at 2024-06-25T09:00Z :white_check_mark:

Rachel: I'll push Helm values to the canary repo and add dashboards for `scale.actions`, `scale.pod-moves`, `cni.attach.latency`.

Ada: If canary looks good we'll roll to us-west1 next week. One ask: do NOT increase `max-empty-bulk-delete` beyond 1 — last time it removed 3 empties concurrently and we had to restore nodes.

Sam: Noted. I'll own the rollback playbook and the runbook steps.

Jess: I'll include the drain annotation for model-serving nodepools: `service.alpha.kubernetes.io/drain-grace=120s`.

Mikel: Example failing logs from last event: \n```
Failed to attach network interface: timeout waiting for ENI
pod/model-xyz: CrashLoopBackOff
```

Ada: Thanks — running the canary now, will post results tomorrow.
